Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient burial mound clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunar November2日}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient burial mound clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient burial mound clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient burial mound clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name= Tsuma Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image= [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunar November2日}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Kokugakuin University’s Shinto and Shrine Historical Data Collection. {{Shinto Horizontal}} [[Category:Shrines Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunar November2日}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群}} * {{ill|Kiki no [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name= Tsuma Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image= [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunar November2日}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Kokugakuin University’s Shinto and Shrine Historical Data Collection. {{Shinto Horizontal}} [[Category:Shrines Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunar November2日}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群}} * {{ill|Kiki no
