[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name= Tsuma Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image= [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|12=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|12=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|12=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|12=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|12=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|12=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|12=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|12=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|12=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|12=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|12=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|12=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|12=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} under the modern shrine ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|12=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|12=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|12=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|12=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|12=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|12=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|12=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|12=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|12=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft|12=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft|12=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|12=draft|12=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|12=draft|12=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|12=draft|12=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|12=draft|12=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft|12=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|12=draft|12=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|12=draft|12=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|12=draft|12=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|12=draft|12=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|12=draft|12=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft|12=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=draft|12=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|12=draft|12=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|12=draft|12=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft|12=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|12=draft|12=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|12=draft|12=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|12=draft|12=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|12=draft|12=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|12=draft|12=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|12=draft|12=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|12=draft|12=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. {{afc comment|1=see [[every:Tsuma Shrine]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:26, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Tsuma Shrine|Tsuma Shrine]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Tsuma Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:36, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Tsuma Shrine|Tsuma Shrine]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Tsuma Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{Promising draft}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name= Tsuma Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image= [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Kokugakuin University’s Shinto and Shrine Historical Data Collection. {{Shinto Horizontal}} [[simple:Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]][[simple:Tsuma Shrine]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{draft categories| }} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:Sōja]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines]] [[Category:Hyūga Province|Shrine 2]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Saito, Miyazaki]] [[Category:History of Saito, Miyazaki]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Tsuma Shrine]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Simple english wikipedia and everybodywiki]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Q11]] }} [[en:draft:Tsuma Shrine]] [[en:Tsuma Shrine]] [[fr:User:Immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[sn:Tsuma Shrine]] [[ja:都萬神社]] [[fr:Tsuma Shrine]] [[sn:suma Shrine]]

Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Kokugakuin University’s Shinto and Shrine Historical Data Collection. {{Shinto Horizontal}} [[simple:Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[simple:user:immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]][[simple:Tsuma Shrine]] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}} {{draft categories| }} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shrines in Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hyūga Province]] [[Category:Sōja]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines]] [[Category:Hyūga Province|Shrine 2]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Saito, Miyazaki]] [[Category:History of Saito, Miyazaki]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category: Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Tsuma Shrine]] [[Category:Pages from Simple English Wikipedia]] [[Category:Simple english wikipedia and everybodywiki]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Q11]] }} [[en:draft:Tsuma Shrine]] [[en:Tsuma Shrine]] [[fr:User:Immanuelle/Tsuma Shrine]] [[sn:Tsuma Shrine]] [[ja:都萬神社]] [[fr:Tsuma Shrine]] [[sn:suma Shrine]]

{{神社 |名称 = 都萬神社 |画像 = [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字妻1 |ISO = JP-45 |緯度度 = 32|緯度分 = 06|緯度秒 = 55.01 |経度度 =131|経度分 = 24|経度秒 = 15.23 |祭神 = [[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花開耶姫命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
[[日向国]][[総社]][[論社]]
日向国[[一宮|二宮]]論社
旧[[県社]] |創建 = 不詳 |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[11月19日]] |神事 = 更衣祭（[[7月7日]]） |地図 = Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鳥居]] '''都萬神社'''（つまじんじゃ、'''都万神社'''）は、[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]で、[[日向国]][[総社]][[論社]]、日向国[[一宮|二宮]]論社。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。「さいまんさま（妻万様）」として親しまれている[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ（pp.18-22）] 一般財団法人 みやざき公園協会、2024年11月26日閲覧。（後述）。 == 社名 == 「都万」の社名について、「妻万」とする説が古くからある『日本の神々』都万神社項。。またその場合、読みを「つま」のほか「さいまん」とする説がある。現在も地元では、「おせんさま」という「さいまん」の転訛による呼称が残っている。 == 祭神 == * '''[[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花開耶姫命]]''' （このはなさくやひめのみこと）祭神は神社由緒書による。 *: 社名の「都万（都萬）」は「妻」のことであり、祭神の木花開耶姫命が[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊]]の妻であることに由来し、社伝によるとこの地が新婚生活の地であるという。 *: 母乳が足りなかったため[[甘酒]]を造ったという伝説があり「日本清酒発祥の地」ともいわれる。神社の南西には「酒元」という集落もある。 一説として、祭神は柧津比売命という説もある。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 創建の年代は不詳。当社周辺には、木花開耶姫命と瓊々杵尊が新婚生活を送ったという伝承地が残っている。当社近くには全国屈指の大古墳群である[[西都原古墳群]]があるほか、屯倉設置の推定地や日向国府跡もあり、日向の中心地であったことがうかがわれる。 都萬神社の神官家の[[日下部氏 (日向国)|日下部氏]]の系図や『妻萬大明神縁起』などによると、瓊瓊杵尊が天下ったころに土から出現した'''日下部立次'''が妻萬大明神を祀ったのが由来であるという西都市史編纂委員会編『西都の歴史』（西都市、1976年）。 なお[[本居宣長]]以来古くから、当地の地名「妻（つま）」を『[[魏志倭人伝]]』に見える「[[投馬国]]」に比定する説がある（確証はされていない）。 === 概史 === 国史の初見は、『[[続日本後紀]]』の[[承和 (日本)|承和]]4年（[[837年]]）8月1日条の「日向国子湯郡[[都農神社|都濃神]]。'''妻神'''。宮埼郡[[江田神社 (宮崎市)|江田神]]。諸県郡[[霧島岑神社|霧島岑神]]。並預官社（都農神社・都萬神社・江田神社・霧島岑神社を官社に預かる）」という記事である。その後、[[神階]]は[[天安 (日本)|天安]]2年（[[858年]]）に従四位下まで昇進した。 『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では日向国[[児湯郡]]に「都万神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している。日向国府は当社近くに設けられており、また「五社明神」という別称から日向国の有力社を合祀していたと見られることから、当社は日向国の[[総社]]の機能を担ったとする説がある{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=631}}。また、都農神社（日向国一宮）に次ぐ二宮として崇敬されたとする説もある{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=631}}江戸時代、高山彦九郎の『筑紫日記』による（『宮崎県の地名』都萬神社項）。。 日向国衙の在庁職にあった日下部氏は当社の神官も務め大きな影響を持ったが、[[室町時代]]以後の当社は[[伊東氏]]から庇護された。中世には「妻宮」「妻万宮」「日向総廟五社大明神」などと呼ばれていたという。日向国の式内社4社の中では、実質的に最も有力な神社であった。 [[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）に、[[近代社格制度]]において[[県社]]に列格し、明治40年（[[1907年]]）には神饌幣帛料供進指定を受けた境内説明板。。 === 神階 === * [[承和 (日本)|承和]]4年（[[837年]]）8月、官社に列格 （『[[続日本後紀]]』） - 表記は「妻神」。 * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]2年（[[858年]]）10月22日、従五位上から従四位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） == 境内 == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|本殿 File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|拝殿 File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|石橋 File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == * 大山祇神社 - 祭神：大山津見命 * 八坂神社 - 祭神：須佐之男命 * 霧島神社 - 祭神：瓊瓊杵命 * 四所神社 - 祭神：磐長姫命ほか3柱 * 稲荷神社 - 祭神：宇迦之御魂命 File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|大山祇神社 File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|八坂神社 == 祭事 == * 歳旦祭 （1月1日）祭事は神社由緒書による。 * 大祓 （6月30日） * 更衣祭 （7月7日） *: 特殊神事。神像に着付けや化粧を施し、祭神・木花開耶姫命の入内までの様子を再現する『宮崎県の地名』都萬神社項。。社伝では日本の婚礼儀礼の初めであるという。 * 例大祭 （11月19日） * 鎮火祭 （旧暦11月2日） * 大祓、除夜祭 （12月31日） == 文化財 == === 国の天然記念物 === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|妻のクス（国の天然記念物）]] * 妻のクス - 推定樹齢は1,200年で、高さ約40メートル。昭和26年6月9日指定[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html 妻のクス]（西都市の文化財）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字妻1 '''交通アクセス''' * [[宮崎交通|宮崎交通バス]]で「都萬神社前」バス停下車 （下車後徒歩すぐ） ** 西都バスセンターからは徒歩約12分。 '''周辺''' * 桜川 - 神社前にある川で世阿弥元清の謡曲『桜川』の前半の舞台であるとする伝承がある。 * [[日向国分寺]] * [[西都原古墳群]] * [[記紀の道]] == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 『日本歴史地名大系 宮崎県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）西都市 都萬神社項 * 中村明蔵「都万神社」（[[谷川健一]]『日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 1 九州』（[[白水社]]）） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|中世諸国一宮制|2000年}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ 都万神社] - 公式サイト * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html 都万神社] - 國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:つましんしや}} [[Category:宮崎県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:宮崎県の旧県社]] [[Category:日向国|社2]] [[Category:西都市の建築物]] [[Category:西都市の歴史]]

{{神社 |名称 = 都萬神社 |画像 = [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字妻1 |ISO = JP-45 |緯度度 = 32|緯度分 = 06|緯度秒 = 55.01 |経度度 =131|経度分 = 24|経度秒 = 15.23 |祭神 = [[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花開耶姫命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
[[日向国]][[総社]][[論社]]
日向国[[一宮|二宮]]論社
旧[[県社]] |創建 = 不詳 |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[11月19日]] |神事 = 更衣祭（[[7月7日]]） |地図 = Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|鳥居]] '''都萬神社'''（つまじんじゃ、'''都万神社'''）は、[[宮崎県]][[西都市]]にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]で、[[日向国]][[総社]][[論社]]、日向国[[一宮|二宮]]論社。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。「さいまんさま（妻万様）」として親しまれている[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ（pp.18-22）] 一般財団法人 みやざき公園協会、2024年11月26日閲覧。（後述）。 == 社名 == 「都万」の社名について、「妻万」とする説が古くからある『日本の神々』都万神社項。。またその場合、読みを「つま」のほか「さいまん」とする説がある。現在も地元では、「おせんさま」という「さいまん」の転訛による呼称が残っている。 == 祭神 == * '''[[コノハナノサクヤビメ|木花開耶姫命]]''' （このはなさくやひめのみこと）祭神は神社由緒書による。 *: 社名の「都万（都萬）」は「妻」のことであり、祭神の木花開耶姫命が[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊]]の妻であることに由来し、社伝によるとこの地が新婚生活の地であるという。 *: 母乳が足りなかったため[[甘酒]]を造ったという伝説があり「日本清酒発祥の地」ともいわれる。神社の南西には「酒元」という集落もある。 一説として、祭神は柧津比売命という説もある。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 創建の年代は不詳。当社周辺には、木花開耶姫命と瓊々杵尊が新婚生活を送ったという伝承地が残っている。当社近くには全国屈指の大古墳群である[[西都原古墳群]]があるほか、屯倉設置の推定地や日向国府跡もあり、日向の中心地であったことがうかがわれる。 都萬神社の神官家の[[日下部氏 (日向国)|日下部氏]]の系図や『妻萬大明神縁起』などによると、瓊瓊杵尊が天下ったころに土から出現した'''日下部立次'''が妻萬大明神を祀ったのが由来であるという西都市史編纂委員会編『西都の歴史』（西都市、1976年）。 なお[[本居宣長]]以来古くから、当地の地名「妻（つま）」を『[[魏志倭人伝]]』に見える「[[投馬国]]」に比定する説がある（確証はされていない）。 === 概史 === 国史の初見は、『[[続日本後紀]]』の[[承和 (日本)|承和]]4年（[[837年]]）8月1日条の「日向国子湯郡[[都農神社|都濃神]]。'''妻神'''。宮埼郡[[江田神社 (宮崎市)|江田神]]。諸県郡[[霧島岑神社|霧島岑神]]。並預官社（都農神社・都萬神社・江田神社・霧島岑神社を官社に預かる）」という記事である。その後、[[神階]]は[[天安 (日本)|天安]]2年（[[858年]]）に従四位下まで昇進した。 『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では日向国[[児湯郡]]に「都万神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している。日向国府は当社近くに設けられており、また「五社明神」という別称から日向国の有力社を合祀していたと見られることから、当社は日向国の[[総社]]の機能を担ったとする説がある{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=631}}。また、都農神社（日向国一宮）に次ぐ二宮として崇敬されたとする説もある{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=631}}江戸時代、高山彦九郎の『筑紫日記』による（『宮崎県の地名』都萬神社項）。。 日向国衙の在庁職にあった日下部氏は当社の神官も務め大きな影響を持ったが、[[室町時代]]以後の当社は[[伊東氏]]から庇護された。中世には「妻宮」「妻万宮」「日向総廟五社大明神」などと呼ばれていたという。日向国の式内社4社の中では、実質的に最も有力な神社であった。 [[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）に、[[近代社格制度]]において[[県社]]に列格し、明治40年（[[1907年]]）には神饌幣帛料供進指定を受けた境内説明板。。 === 神階 === * [[承和 (日本)|承和]]4年（[[837年]]）8月、官社に列格 （『[[続日本後紀]]』） - 表記は「妻神」。 * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]2年（[[858年]]）10月22日、従五位上から従四位下 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） == 境内 == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|本殿 File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|拝殿 File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|石橋 File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|一の鳥居 == 摂末社 == * 大山祇神社 - 祭神：大山津見命 * 八坂神社 - 祭神：須佐之男命 * 霧島神社 - 祭神：瓊瓊杵命 * 四所神社 - 祭神：磐長姫命ほか3柱 * 稲荷神社 - 祭神：宇迦之御魂命 File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|大山祇神社 File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|八坂神社 == 祭事 == * 歳旦祭 （1月1日）祭事は神社由緒書による。 * 大祓 （6月30日） * 更衣祭 （7月7日） *: 特殊神事。神像に着付けや化粧を施し、祭神・木花開耶姫命の入内までの様子を再現する『宮崎県の地名』都萬神社項。。社伝では日本の婚礼儀礼の初めであるという。 * 例大祭 （11月19日） * 鎮火祭 （旧暦11月2日） * 大祓、除夜祭 （12月31日） == 文化財 == === 国の天然記念物 === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|妻のクス（国の天然記念物）]] * 妻のクス - 推定樹齢は1,200年で、高さ約40メートル。昭和26年6月9日指定[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html 妻のクス]（西都市の文化財）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[宮崎県]][[西都市]]大字妻1 '''交通アクセス''' * [[宮崎交通|宮崎交通バス]]で「都萬神社前」バス停下車 （下車後徒歩すぐ） ** 西都バスセンターからは徒歩約12分。 '''周辺''' * 桜川 - 神社前にある川で世阿弥元清の謡曲『桜川』の前半の舞台であるとする伝承がある。 * [[日向国分寺]] * [[西都原古墳群]] * [[記紀の道]] == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 『日本歴史地名大系 宮崎県の地名』（[[平凡社]]）西都市 都萬神社項 * 中村明蔵「都万神社」（[[谷川健一]]『日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 1 九州』（[[白水社]]）） * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|中世諸国一宮制|2000年}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ 都万神社] - 公式サイト * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html 都万神社] - 國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:つましんしや}} [[Category:宮崎県の神社]] [[Category:日向国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:宮崎県の旧県社]] [[Category:日向国|社2]] [[Category:西都市の建築物]] [[Category:西都市の歴史]]

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name= Tsuma Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image= [[File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-front view.jpg|280px]]
Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Saitobaru Kofuns|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - Kyushu,'' Kenichi Tanigawa, editor, Hakusuisha). * {{Cite book|editor=Medieval Provincial Sōja Research Group|title=The Fundamental Study of Medieval Provincial Sōja|publisher=Iwata Shoin|year=2000|isbn=978-4872941708}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsuma-jinja}} * [https://tsumajinja.webnode.jp/ Tsuma Shrine Official Website] * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/640201.html Tsuma Shrine] - Main Hall |location= {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (small), {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Established= Unknown |festival= {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |Rituals= Kōrōsai ({{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|ja|日向国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|ja|甘酒|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|ja|西都原古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|ja|本居宣長|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|ja|魏志倭人伝|lt=Gishiwajinden|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|ja|伊東氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - New Year's Festival * {{ill|June 30|ja|6月30日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae (Great Purification) * {{ill|July 7|ja|7月7日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * {{ill|November 19|ja|11月19日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * {{ill|December 31|ja|12月31日|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|ja|西都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|ja|宮崎県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center.
