Main Hall |location= [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]] Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (small), [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} |Established= Unknown |festival= [[:en:November 19|November 19]] |Rituals= Kōrōsai ([[:en:July 7|July 7]]) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]], [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]], [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|1=Miyazaki Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11454180}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. Main Hall |location= [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]] Oaza Tsuma 1 |ISO= JP-45 |coordinates= {{coord|32|06|55.01|N|131|24|15.23|E|display=inline}} |deity= {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} |type= {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (small), [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (disputed), Second Shrine (disputed), {{ill|Former Prefectural Shrine|ja|旧県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Former Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} |Established= Unknown |festival= [[:en:November 19|November 19]] |Rituals= Kōrōsai ([[:en:July 7|July 7]]) |Map= Japan Miyazaki }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]], [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]], Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - New Year's Festival * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Ōharae (Great Purification) * [[:en:July 7|July 7]] - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * [[:en:November 19|November 19]] - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|qq=}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|qq=}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. File:Tsuma-jinja Ooyamazumi-jinja.JPG|Ōyamazumi Shrine File:Tsuma-jinja Yasaka-jinja.JPG|Yasaka Shrine == Festivals == * [[:en:January 1|January 1]] - New Year's Festival * [[:en:June 30|June 30]] - Ōharae (Great Purification) * [[:en:July 7|July 7]] - Kōrōsai (special ceremony reenacting Konohanasakuya-hime's bridal journey) * [[:en:November 19|November 19]] - festival * {{ill|Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja|Lunisolar November2日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Traditional Lunar Calendar November 2|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} - Chinka Festival (Fire Pacification) * [[:en:December 31|December 31]] - Ōharae and Year-End Festival == Cultural Properties == === National Natural Monument === [[File:Tsuma-jinja kusunoki.JPG|thumb|180px|right|Tsuma no Kusu (National Natural Monument)]] * '''Tsuma no Kusu''' - A camphor tree approximately 1,200 years old and 40 meters tall. Designated in 1951 (Showa 26).[http://www.city.saito.miyazaki.jp/contents/syakai/bunkazai/tennen/1.html Tsuma no Kusu - Saito City Cultural Assets]. == Visitor Information == '''Address''' * Oaza Tsuma 1, [[:en:Saito, Miyazaki|Saito, Miyazaki]], [[:en:Miyazaki Prefecture|Miyazaki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * {{ill|Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|ja|宮崎交通|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazaki Kotsu Bus|1=Miyazaki Kotsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11454180}} - Alight at "Tsuma Shrine-mae" bus stop (short walk). * Approximately 12 minutes on foot from the Saito Bus Center. '''Nearby Attractions''' * {{ill|Sakuragawa River|ja|桜川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakuragawa River|1=Sakuragawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11538014}} - Featured in the Noh play ''Sakuragawa.'' * {{ill|Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja|日向国分寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyūga Kokubun-ji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日向国分寺跡|1=Hyūga Kokubun-ji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11505107}} * [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofuns]] * {{ill|Kiki no Michi|ja|記紀の道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiki no Michi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Kiki-no-michi|WD=Q63214841}} == References == {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine's historical pamphlets * ''Miyazaki Prefecture Place names,'' Heibonsha, entry on Tsuma Shrine. * Akira Nakamaura, ''Tsuma Shrine'' (in ''Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 1 - It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] and the second shrine of [[:en:Hyūga Province|Hyūga Province]]. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made [[:en:Amazake|Amazake]], leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and [[:en:Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the [[:en:Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster]], one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of [[:en:Motoori Norinaga|Motoori Norinaga]], the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''[[:en:Wajinden|Gishiwajinden]].'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''[[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Zoku Nihon Kōki]]'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the [[:en:Itō clan|Itō clan]]. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''[[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto.
