|prefecture= {{ill|Saito|WD=Q850479|1=Saito, Miyazaki}} }} [[File:Tsuma-jinja entrance.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii gate]] '''Tsuma Shrine''' (都萬神社 or 都万神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Saito, Miyazaki|en|Saito, Miyazaki|WD=Q850479|lt=Saito, Miyazaki|1=Saito, Miyazaki}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|en|Miyazaki Prefecture|WD=Q130300|lt=Miyazaki Prefecture|1=Miyazaki Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} and is associated with the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} and the second shrine of {{ill|Hyūga Province|en|Hyūga Province|WD=Q513737|lt=Hyūga Province|1=Hyūga Province}}. Known locally as "Saimansama," it is beloved by the community.[https://mppf.or.jp/wpsys/wp-content/themes/mppf/docs/saito/marukajiriMapP18.pdf 西都まるかじりマップ・西都周遊マップ (pp.18-22)] Miyazaki Parks Association, retrieved November 26, 2024. == name == The name "Tsuma" (都萬 or 都万) is believed to mean "wife" (妻) and refers to the connection between the shrine's deity, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}, and her husband, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|1=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}. Locally, the shrine is also affectionately called "Osensama," a derivation of "Saiman."From the entry on Tsuma Shrine in ''Japanese Gods''. == Deities == * '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}}''' (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)The shrine's official records. *: The name "Tsuma" reflects her role as the wife of Ninigi-no-Mikoto, and legend holds that this location was the site of their newlywed life. *: A legend claims that, due to a lack of breast milk, she made {{ill|Amazake|en|Amazake|WD=Q455990|lt=Amazake|1=Amazake}}, leading to the claim that this is the birthplace of Japanese sake brewing. A nearby settlement, "Sakaguchi" (酒元), further supports this claim. Some theories propose that the enshrined deity may instead be Kokutsu-hime-no-Mikoto. == History == === Foundation === The founding date is unknown, but the surrounding area is rich with legends of {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花開耶姫命|1=Konohanasakuya-hime|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Konohanasakuya-hime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to コノハナノサクヤビメ}} and {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|1=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}'s life together. Nearby are significant historical sites such as the {{ill|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|en|Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|WD=Q3469314|lt=Saitobaru Kofun Cluster|1=Saitobaru Kofun Cluster}}, one of Japan's most important ancient Kofun clusters, as well as the proposed location of the Hyūga provincial office and regional rice storehouses. According to the genealogical records of the {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, the shrine was founded by "Kusakabe Tatsutsugi," who worshipped the deity of "Tsuma Myōjin" during Ninigi-no-Mikoto's descent from heaven.''History of Saito,'' compiled by the Saito Historical Compilation Committee, 1976. Since the time of {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|en|Motoori Norinaga|WD=Q384647|lt=Motoori Norinaga|1=Motoori Norinaga}}, the name "Tsuma" has been linked with the "Toma Province" mentioned in the ''{{ill|Wajinden|en|Wajinden|WD=Q1135798|lt=Gishiwajinden|1=Wajinden}}.'' However, this theory remains unconfirmed. === Historical Overview === The first mention of the shrine in historical records is from ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|WD=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki|1=Shoku Nihon Kōki}}'' (837 CE), which refers to "Tsuma Shrine" being designated as an official government shrine. The shrine's Rank rose to {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|Junior Fourth Rank=Junior Fourth Rank|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fourth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従四位}} in 858 CE. In the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}, the shrine is listed as a minor shrine in Hyūga Province's Koyu District. It is believed to have served as a provincial {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} due to its location near the provincial office and its role as the site of multiple deities' worship. Some records also suggest it was revered as Hyūga's second shrine. The {{ill|Kusakabe clan|ja|日下部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusakabe clan (Hyūga Province)|qq=}}, who served as both the provincial administrators and shrine priests, maintained significant influence over the shrine. However, during the medieval period, the shrine came under the patronage of the {{ill|Itō clan|en|Itō clan|WD=Q2975280|lt=Itō clan|1=Itō clan}}. In 1873 (Meiji 6), the shrine was officially designated as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|1=Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Historical types === * 837 CE: Designated as a government shrine (''Zoku Nihon Kōki''). * 858 CE: Promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}''). == Grounds == File:Tsuma-jinja honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Tsuma-jinja haiden-diagonal view.jpg|Haiden (worship hall) File:Tsuma-jinja ishibashi.JPG|Stone Bridge File:Tsuma-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii Gate == Sub-Shrines == * '''Ōyamazumi Shrine''' - Enshrines Ōyama-tsumi-no-Mikoto. * '''Yasaka Shrine''' - Enshrines Susanoo-no-Mikoto. * '''Kirishima Shrine''' - Enshrines Ninigi-no-Mikoto. * '''Shisho Shrine''' - Enshrines Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto and three others. * '''Inari Shrine''' - Enshrines Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto.
